question: Is a two-point attitude BVP shoot (solve ω that connects q_a→q_b under torque-free dynamics) well-posed, how many roots connect a pair, and does it beat finite-diff ω under anchor noise?
hypothesis: A large-Δt BVP solve removes the constant-ω/polhode-drift error of finite-diff and is better conditioned against anchor noise.
narrative_md: Built and validated lib/shoot.py: a two-point attitude BVP solver that LM-solves the body-frame ω connecting q_a→q_b under torque-free dynamics. Primitive validated (round-trip 1.7e-6°); multiplicity is real but tamed by a ±30% |ω| prior (truth unique on slow seed to 241°, fast to ~160°). BVP decisively beats finite-diff on fast tumblers under q-cloud noise (ω-dir ~1.5-2.4° vs finite-diff 80-127°), clearing the s087 1.25° gate for σ_q≲2.0°. Uses perturbed-truth pairs → not blind.
